autoWah: An envelope wah: the louder you play, the higher the peak sweeps.
fuzzWah: Fuzz-Wah: a wah (Classic, Retro, Modern, Opto 1 and 2, Resonant LP/HP, Peak) moved by the playing's level (depth, attack, release, range) with relative Q and auto gain; a compressor (ratio); a fuzz (gain, tone); and the order the three come in.
spectralGate: Spectral Gate: a band (centre frequency and bandwidth, both wobbled at Speed by CF and BW Modulation) split from the rest; the band's parts above the threshold (Super Energy) and below it (Sub Energy) at their own levels; the original lows and highs either side mixed back; gain.
formantBank: Formant Filterbank: two banks of up to 20 band-pass filters between the lowest and highest frequency, each band's level set in bank A and bank B, crossfaded (Fade AB); formant shift, resonance, slope, the lowest band band-pass or high-pass and the highest band-pass or low-pass; a Shift LFO and a Fade LFO (rate, wave, intensity); overdrive, level, stereo width.
stepFilter: Eight steps of cutoff, one per note value, gliding or jumping, in time with the song.
stereoSpread: Widens by sending alternate frequency bands left and right (mono-compatible: it only adds side).
directionMixer: Direction Mixer: an LR or MS input, the direction its centre points to (degrees: 90 hard left, -90 hard right, beyond that turning back) and its spread (0 mono, 1 as is, 2 only the sides); Split gives the lows and highs (either side of the crossover) their own direction and spread.
testOsc: A test tone, noise or a sweep, in place of (or added to) the track.
vocoder: The classic vocoder: the track's spectrum (bands followed) shapes a carrier - the side chain or a built-in synth.
exciter: Adds brightness: new harmonics made from the highs only.
denoiser: Spectral noise reduction: each frequency below the threshold is turned down, smoothly over time.
stereoDelay: Stereo Delay: each side its own input (Off, Left, Right, L+R, L-R), time or note with deviation, feedback with phase, crossfeed to the other side with phase; the routing presets (Straight, Crossfeed, 90/10, 10/90, Ping Pong, Pan, Rotate) or Customized; low and high cut on the echoes; output level per side, width, dry/wet mix.
tapeDelay: Tape Delay: time or note with deviation, feedback, Freeze, low and high cut in the loop, the tape's LFO and flutter (each a rate and an intensity) evened out by Smoothing, a clip threshold for the tape's saturation, Clean or Diffuse head, spread, dry and wet.
modDelay: Modulation Delay: a short delay swept by two LFOs (left and right rates, or linked, mixed), with feedback; De-Warble keeps the pitch steady (the sweep moves between two fixed taps instead of bending the delay), Constant Mod keeps the sweep's width the same at any rate, D-Mode's spatial filtering; stereo phase and its distribution, a low/high cut filter, volume modulation, mix.
echo: A simple echo: time (or a note), repeats and a colour knob from dark to bright.
sampleDelay: Delays each side by a number of samples (to line up mics, or for the Haas widening trick).
guitarAmp: Amp Designer: 24 amps, 25 cabinets (and Direct), an EQ type for the tone stack, gain, bass, mids, treble, presence, master; spring and studio reverbs (ten types, level); tremolo or vibrato (depth, speed or synced); seven microphones, where they point and how close; output.
bassAmp: Bass Amp Designer: three amps (Classic, Flip Top, Modern), eight cabinets (and the two Direct outs), three microphones with their position; channel I/II, Bright, gain, bass/mids/treble with the Low, 1-2-3 and High switches, master; a compressor (hard/soft, amount, gain); an extra EQ (graphic, or two parametric bands), before or after the compressor; a D.I. box (boost, HF cut, six tone curves) blended with the amp; output.
chorus: Chorus: rate, intensity, delay, voices, spread, feedback, D-Mode, mix.
ensemble: Ensemble: up to eight voices modulated by LFO 1, LFO 2 and a random source (each on/off, rate, intensity), spread across the stereo field, their phases offset, volume compensation, mix.
microphaser: Microphaser: a small, simple phaser - rate (or synced), intensity, feedback.
phaser: Phaser: 4 to 12 stages (odd numbers: comb filtering), the sweep between Floor and Ceiling by two LFOs (each its rate or a note, mixed), or by the input's envelope; the stereo phase and its distribution; feedback level, Warmth, a low/high cut filter, output mix.
tremolo: Tremolo: rate (or a note), depth, the wave's smoothing and symmetry, its offset, and the left-right phase with its distribution.
autoPan: Auto Pan: equal-power balance swung left and right in a chosen shape.
rotary: Rotor Cabinet: Slow, Brake or Fast; the cabinet (Wood, Proline, Single, Split, and their "& Horn IR" versions); acceleration and maximum rate; motor control (Normal, Inverse, 910, Sync); the horn's and drum's microphones (Dynamic, Condenser or Mid-Side), front or rear, distance, angle, horn/drum balance, and the horn's and drum's width.
ringMod: Ringshifter: a frequency shifter (one shift, or opposite shifts left and right) or a ring modulator (by its sine oscillator, or by the side chain). The oscillator's frequency, moved by the envelope follower and the LFO; a delay (or synced) with its level; the envelope follower (sensitivity, attack, decay) and the LFO (symmetry, smoothing, rate or synced); then dry/wet (also moved by the envelope and LFO), feedback and stereo width.
scannerVibrato: Scanner Vibrato: V1-V3 vibrato (only the scanned line heard) or C0-C3 chorus (scanned and dry together); depth, stereo phase, left and right rates.
vibrato: Pitch wobble: a short delay swept, heard alone (no dry).
channelEq: Channel EQ: the eight bands on both channels or just one side (Left, Right, Mid or Side); HQ runs them at twice the rate (no cramping near the top); the analyzer reads before or after.
delayDesigner: Delay Designer: up to 26 taps (A to Z), each with its own time, level, pan, transposition, filter, flip and mute; taps can snap to a tempo grid with swing, and one tap feeds back.
subBass: An octave (or two) below the bass, made from its zero crossings and following its level.
spreader: Wider: each side a few milliseconds apart and a few cents apart, gently moving.
overdrive: A pedal-style overdrive: mids pushed into a soft, slightly uneven clip, then a tone control.
distortion: Harder distortion: lots of gain into a sharper clip.
distortion2: Distortion II: pre gain, drive and tone (a high shelf before and after) through one of five circuits - Growl (a two-stage tube amp), Bity (an overdriven blues amp), Nasty (hard), Class AB soft and hard (transistor crossover distortion) - then output, mix and level compensation.
phaseDistortion: Phase Distortion: the input's lows (a resonant low pass at Cutoff) bend a short delay on the signal itself, so its own bass moves its phase; Intensity, the delay's reach, Phase Reverse (the right channel moves the other way), Monitor (hear just the filter), mix.
fuzz: Fuzz: a biased, nearly square clip with a gate for the hiss between notes.
bitcrusher: Fewer bits and a lower sample rate (aliasing on purpose), with a drive and fold/clip/wrap at the top.
clipDistortion: Clip Distortion: input gain, drive into an asymmetric clip (Symmetry) through its clip filter, then a high shelf (frequency and gain) and a low pass, mix and output.
saturator: Saturator: five models - Retro Tube, Modern Tube, Magnetic (tape), Squeeze (pushed compression) and Analog Preamp - each with two styles (clean or colourful; soft or hard press), drive, Bypass Below (the lows left untouched under a frequency), level in and out, mix, and low and high cut filters (slope, resonance, before or after the saturation).
levelMeter: Level Meter: peak and RMS of each side, with the highest peak held (for the window).
loudnessMeter: Loudness Meter: M, S and I in LUFS, the loudness range in LU, the true peak; Start/Pause and Reset.
correlationMeter: Correlation Meter: +1 in phase (mono), 0 wide, -1 out of phase.
multiMeter: MultiMeter: a 31-band third-octave analyzer, a goniometer, correlation and peak levels.
tuner: Tuner: the note played and how far off it is, against the reference pitch.
bpmCounter: BPM Counter: the tempo found from the onsets of what's playing.
masteringAssistant: Mastering Assistant: listens to the mix (the first 30 seconds played after Reanalyze), then sets a corrective EQ (Auto EQ, how much of it), the gain to reach the loudness you choose, and runs the mix through a character - Clean, Valve, Punch or Transparent - into a true peak limiter at -1 dBTP; Excite adds upper-mid saturation, Width moves the sides (above 150 Hz), a custom EQ (low, mid, high); Loudness Compensation plays it back at the original loudness for a fair comparison.
aVerb: AVerb: one Density/Time control for both the reflections and the tail.
goldVerb: GoldVerb: early reflections from a room of 3 to 7 corners, and a separate tail, balanced.
silverComp: Silver Compressor: threshold, ratio, attack, release, a soft knee and makeup gain.
silverGate: Silver Gate: below the threshold the sound drops by the reduction, with attack, hold and release, and lookahead.
deesserLegacy: The original DeEsser: a detector band and a separate suppressor band; strength, smoothing, monitors.
speechEnhancer: Speech Enhancer: noise taken down, the microphone's colour corrected, the voice brought forward.
grooveshifter: Grooveshifter: swing put into straight playing - every other eighth (or sixteenth) moved later, without changing the pitch (grains of the sound played at their speed while time is stretched and squeezed).
guitarAmpPro: Guitar Amp Pro: its amps, speakers and EQs are among Amp Designer's.
bassAmpLegacy: The original Bass Amp: its amps and controls, played by Bass Amp Designer.
pitchCorrection: Pitch correction: each note pulled to the nearest note of the key, as fast as the Response says.
vocalTransformer: Pitch and formants moved on their own (a deeper voice that isn't slowed, a higher one that isn't a chipmunk), or a robot.
pitchShifter: Shifts anything (chords, drums) by two crossfading delay taps sweeping through a window.
multiband: Multipressor: four bands split by three crossovers (phase-matched), each with its own compression (threshold, ratio), downward expansion (threshold, ratio, reduction), peak/RMS detection time, attack, release, make-up gain, on/off and solo; auto gain, lookahead and output.
deesser: DeEsser 2: a detection filter (high shelf or peak) at Frequency; Relative mode compares the band with the whole signal (steady whatever the level), Absolute with a fixed threshold; Max Reduction caps it; Split turns down just the band, Wide the whole signal; Filter Solo plays the band.
noiseGate: Noise Gate: Gate (closes below the threshold) or Ducker (turns down while the key is loud); threshold, reduction, hysteresis, attack, hold, release, lookahead; the key's filter (band pass or band reject between its low and high cutoff) with Monitor to hear it.
expander: Expander: above the threshold the signal is made louder still (upward expansion, by the ratio) - or, Downward, below it quieter, down to the range; knee, attack, release, Peak or RMS detection, gain with Auto Gain, and an output clip (Off, Soft, Hard, Clip).
enveloper: Enveloper: turns the attack of each sound up or down, and its release up or down, whatever its level: the threshold sets what counts, Lookahead reads ahead, Release Time how long the tail lasts, Out Level the result.
transient: More or less attack and sustain, whatever the level (two envelope followers, compared).
brickwall: Limiter: looks ahead so peaks are caught before they arrive - nothing goes over the output level. Gain in, release, lookahead; Legacy (with an optional soft knee) or Precision (with optional true peak detection, catching the peaks between samples); a Warm character option.
adaptiveLimiter: Adaptive Limiter: raises the level and rounds the peaks off like a well-driven analog stage, never above the ceiling; its release adapts (quick for transients, slower for dense music). Gain, Out Ceiling, Lookahead, Remove DC Offset, True Peak Detection.
remixFx: A DJ-style multi-effect: two XY pads, a gater and a downsampler, reverse, scratch and tape stop.
beatBreaker: Beat Breaker: the incoming audio, a pattern long, played back in slices - each from its own place in the input, at its own speed (backwards too), repeated, filtered, faded and panned.
plateReverb: The classic plate (Jon Dattorro's 1997 design): a figure-of-eight tank with modulated diffusers.
springReverb: A spring tank: a chain of all-passes spreads each sound into the spring's chirp, round a feedback loop.
convSpace: Convolution with an impulse response made from the knobs (built again, off the audio thread, when they move).
platinumVerb: PlatinumVerb: early reflections from a room of 3 to 7 corners, its size, the stereo base of the two microphones and an ER scale; then the tail - initial delay, spread, two bands (crossover, low ratio, low level), high cut, density, diffusion, reverb time - and the balance.
enVerb: EnVerb: a reverb shaped by an envelope - attack, decay to the sustain level, hold, then release - started by each new phrase; the dry signal can be delayed; density, spread, high cut, a crossover with the low band's level, dry and wet.
silverVerb: SilverVerb: predelay, reflectivity, size, density/time, low and high cut, and an LFO (on/off, rate, left-right phase, intensity) that wobbles the tail; dry and wet.
autoFilter: AutoFilter: a resonant filter (HP, BP, LP, or a 4-pole low pass of 6 to 24 dB/oct) with Fatness and stereo Spread; its cutoff moved by an ADSR envelope (started above the threshold, scaled by Dynamic) and by an LFO (six waves, pulse width, rate or synced with phase, stereo phase, retrigger); distortion before and after the filter; dry signal and main out.
linearEq: Linear Phase EQ: the same eight bands as the Channel EQ (low and high cut with slopes up to 48 dB/oct, two shelves, four bells), but as a linear-phase filter, so nothing is shifted in time - the choice for mastering and for parallel or multi-mic sources. It adds a little latency.
studioComp: Studio Compressor: seven circuits (Platinum Digital, Studio VCA, Studio FET, Classic VCA, Vintage VCA, Vintage FET, Vintage Opto), each with its own detector, timing, knee and colour. Threshold, ratio, attack, release, knee, make-up and Auto Gain; a side-chain filter (LP, BP, HP, ParEQ, HS) with Listen, Max or Sum and Peak or RMS detection; on the way out a limiter, Soft/Hard/Clip distortion and a dry/wet Mix for parallel compression.
eq: The simple three-band EQ: a low shelf, a mid bell (with Q) and a high shelf, each with its frequency and gain (up to 18 dB).
compressor: The simple compressor: threshold, ratio, attack, release and make-up gain - all a vocal or a bass usually needs. The meter shows the gain reduction.
delay: The simple delay: a time, how much of each echo comes back (feedback) and the dry/wet mix.
reverb: The simple reverb: room size, damping (darker tail), stereo width and mix.
limiter: The simple limiter: nothing goes past the ceiling; release sets how quickly it lets go.
singleEq: One band of EQ, of the type you choose: low cut, high cut, low shelf, high shelf, bell, notch or band pass, with its frequency, gain, Q and (for the cuts) a 12 or 24 dB/oct slope.
consoleEq: A British-console style EQ: a stepped high pass, a low shelf (four frequencies), a mid bell (six frequencies) and a 12 kHz high shelf, with a drive that adds the circuit's colour, and output.
graphicEq: A ten-band graphic EQ, one slider per octave from 31 Hz to 16 kHz, and output. Quick broad tone shaping.
tubeEq: A passive tube program EQ: low boost and low attenuation at the same frequency (boost both for the famous tight low end), a high boost with its bandwidth, a separate high attenuation, and output through the tube stage.
studioReverb: Studio Reverb: an algorithmic reverb with eight room types (Room, Chamber, Concert Hall, Theater, Synth Hall, Digital, Dark Room, Dense Room). Size, decay, predelay (or a note), attack, distance, density, modulation, width and the early/late balance; a four-band decay EQ (how long each range rings), Freeze, a mono maker for the lows and a five-band output EQ.
flanger: Flanger: a very short delay swept by an LFO (rate or a note value), with intensity, feedback for the jet sound, stereo phase and mix.
gain: Gain: level up or down, invert the phase of either side, swap left and right, sum to mono (or keep just the left or right), and balance. The utility for fixing polarity and checking mono.
matchEq: Match EQ: learns the average spectrum of a reference (a song you like - the Template) and of your track (Current), then sets a filter that makes yours sound like it. Apply sets how much (negative values do the opposite), Smoothing how fine the curve is, Phase linear or minimum; four bands of your own on top.
pedalboard: Pedalboard: a chain of up to six stomp boxes, in order, each switched on or off with its three knobs. 23 pedals: fuzz, octave fuzz, overdrive, tube drive, distortion, grinder, bit crusher, compressor, chorus, flanger, phaser, microphaser, tremolo, vibrato, scanner vibrato, rotary, auto wah, fuzz wah, tape delay, echo, spring reverb, ring shifter and pitch.
phatFx: Phat FX: six effects in an order you choose - a band pass, a filter (ladder, classic and phat types), a distortion (eight types, in three stages), modulation, a bass enhancer and a compressor - with input, output, mix and a soft or hard limiter. Two LFOs, an envelope follower and an XY pad move them. Makes drums, basses and synths bigger and dirtier.
stepFx: Step FX: a filter, distortion, modulation, delay and reverb, moved by three step sequencers in time with the song (gate, cutoff, resonance, amounts) and by an XY pad you can play live. Rhythmic gating and moving filters for loops, pads and builds.
roomSim: Room Simulator: a classic digital room algorithm (Classic or Modern). Reverb time, room size, density, predelay, the first reflections' level, delay and spread, high cut, a bass band (gain and crossover), correlation patterns for each side, Freeze, and the dry, early and reverb levels.
